verdict.rationale: Fly.io clearly documents managed full-stack app deployment. `fly launch` creates, configures and deploys apps, generates Dockerfiles for popular frameworks, and pairs apps with fully managed Postgres; Machines boot fast, scale out, and Sprites sleep at zero compute cost. However, the platform is built on VMs you explicitly create and manage the lifecycle of, and there is no documented serverless-function model. Community reports of flaky deploys lower confidence but do not contradict that the capability exists. Missing for 10: a documented serverless/function-as-a-service deployment model, evidence of a truly no-servers-to-manage abstraction (users control Machine lifecycle, resources and placement), and independent corroboration of smooth deploys.

support.subject: As a developer, I can deploy serverless functions and full-stack apps with no servers to manage

citations.quote: Run `fly launch` from inside your project source directory to create, configure, and (for most apps) deploy a new application.
No Dockerfile? No problem: we'll generate one for most popular frameworks, including Rails, Phoenix, Django, Node, Laravel, Go, Rust, .NET and more.
Host the web apps you and your agents build, with Postgres and storage.
Fly.io's Managed Postgres is our fully-managed database service that handles all aspects of running production PostgreSQL databases
Fly Machines are hardware-isolated VMs that boot in under a second, run close to your users, and scale out to tens of thousands when the traffic arrives.
It sleeps (at zero compute cost) until you wake it on request.
